title.narrative: PIMS_6738_Integrated Program for HFC Phasing Down and Sustainable Cooling for Tajikistan

description.narrative: Brief project description: The project objective is to support Tajikistan in meeting its Montreal Protocol KigaliAmendment obligation to rapidly reduce consumption of HFC by 70% in 2029. This widely used coolinginfrastructure refrigerant as well as an insulating foam blowing agent has high global warming potential (GWP)and is a major contributor to global warming when emitted to the atmosphere. Tajikistan has a significantlygreater HFC consumption obligations relative to similar countries given its status as a developed rather thandeveloping country under the Montreal Protocol. Meeting this challenge will involve the accelerated replacementof existing cooling equipment and adoption of available low GWP/high energy efficiency alternatives. The projectis designed to direct GEF support to the country based on an integrated strategy combining i) aggressiveintroduction of progressive import controls on HFCs and HFC based equipment; ii) restricting emissions andconserving refrigerant through development of life cycle refrigerant management (LRM) practices and introducingmonitoring techniques to optimize equipment operation; iii) leveraging investment in accelerated coolingequipment replacement through demonstration of modern cooling technology; and iv) facilitating innovativefinancial incentives for expanded new investment by end users. An integral part of this will be strengtheningexpanded institutional and refrigeration servicing capacity human resource in the form of training and equipment.In terms global environmental benefit, the project is estimated to eliminate 2,096,043 t CO2Eq in direct HFCemissions and 740,700 t CO2 Eq indirect emissions through energy efficiency improvements as well as reduce HFC chemical demand by 903 t that would otherwise be released during its implementation period alone.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
